elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: 18.1 retains an evergreen continuation: the Agreement "shall continue in operation for at least an initial period of twenty-five (25) years ... and shall be terminable thereafter by agreement of the Parties." Continuation past the Initial Period is automatic (it persists until a Party gives notice), not conditioned on a fresh mutual written renewal agreement, and the conditional auto-renewal elements below are not all satisfied.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause sets no renewal term at all — the Agreement simply "continue[s] in operation" indefinitely after the 25-year Initial Period. No 12-month renewal term was inserted.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered text gives "not less than sixty (60) days' prior notice" — 60 days exceeds the 30-day preferred ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered 18.1/18.3; the redline adds none and the comment does not promise one.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Paragraph 18 contains no renewal or continuation price-uplift mechanic (cost sharing runs on actual Capital/O&M Costs under Schedule B), so there is no increase to cap.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Operative language as rendered: "any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter by giving not less than sixty (60) days' prior notice thereof, in writing" — the exit window is exactly 60 days, at the fallback ceiling, replacing the original one (1) year (365-day) window.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — Paragraph 18 as rendered contains no price-increase or uplift mechanic on continuation. (The mapping labels this "already_met" and quotes the duration sentence, which is not a pricing provision; the element is nonetheless satisfied because the condition is not engaged.)

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level: the single numeric edit brings the unilateral exit window from one (1) year to sixty (60) days, and the price-cap element is not engaged because Paragraph 18 contains no continuation/renewal uplift mechanic.

Preferred level remains unmet on three operative points, which under the reading convention are noted rather than separately redlined: no defined 12-month renewal term (continuation is indefinite), opt-out at 60 rather than 30 days, and no Vendor reminder obligation 60 days before renewal.

Minimality holds: the only textual change is the numeral in the second sentence of 18.1; the "terminable thereafter by agreement of the Parties" language, the Initial Period, and 18.3's two-thirds decommissioning vote are retained verbatim, with no added survival tails, procedures, or extras.

Intent preserved: no undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence results; the decommissioning and realization-of-assets mechanics in 18.3 continue to operate unchanged.

Caution to flag with the client (not a verification defect): the notice right in 18.1 is mutual ("any Party"), so shortening it to 60 days also lets other Parties exit the consortium on 60 days' notice, which may destabilize cost-sharing and voting interests under Schedule B. If that reciprocity is unacceptable, the alternative is an asymmetric Customer-only shortening, but that would add scope beyond the fallback checklist.

Substantive check of the deterministic evidence confirms the regex result: the rendered figure is sixty (60) days in the operative exit sentence, not merely in the comment, and no competing longer notice period survives in the cited text.
